name: @olai/plugin-api
//name: IT WAS `@olai/plugins`, in `packages/plugins/`, and the rename is what made room for the tenants. `packages/plugins/` is the tenant CONTAINER now — one directory holding `olai-plugin-kolu`, `olai-plugin-odu` and `olai-plugin-xyne-spaces` and nothing else — so the interface could not stay in it: this is the one package a plugin may not import, and a directory that held both the fence's subject and the thing it fences reads as a contradiction in the workspace globs and in the fence's own graph walk. `plugin-api` is what the thing is: the interface a manifest is written against, plus the registry that is the one place either tenant's name is spelled.
//exports: Three entries, and the split is the one this package exists to make: three doors because three GRAPHS. `./wire` is the BROWSER-SAFE half — the sibling map, the filters and the fusion helpers — on a graph that reaches each plugin's own `./wire` subpath and stops there. `@olai/server`'s composition root reads it today and `@olai/web`'s composed client is what it is kept browser-safe FOR, which is why the fence holds it to two claims at once: no UI runtime reaches a server through it, and no appliance client reaches a browser. `./server` is what a COMPOSITION ROOT reads to build a runtime: each plugin's server half, which pulls its appliance client and the vault walks it runs, and no browser face. The root is the MANIFESTS whole — the probes, the dressings and the chrome, which are SolidJS components and, behind kolu's, a terminal emulator. A single door would put those on the static graph of every listener that reads the surface AND on every server that renders nothing, which is the exact hazard `@olai/kolu-client/wire`'s own fence was written for, one floor down. src/fence.test.ts walks each closure rather than trusting this sentence. A FOURTH entry is not a fourth graph: `./all.css` is the plugins' stylesheets chained, and it is here because a CSS import is a door a plugin's name can be spelled through — the fence reads a `.css` file's imports for exactly that reason, so the app imports one line and names no tenant. A FIFTH, `./testids`, is the same routing for the same reason in a third grammar: a `data-testid` is spent in `@olai/tests`, which may not name a plugin either, and the door is NAMES ONLY so a suite with no browser in it never pulls a component.
//: THE ONLY PLACE CORE MEETS PLUGINS — see src/plugin.ts, which argues the interface, and src/registry.ts, which argues why the registry is a source file rather than a data structure. What this manifest is FOR is the direction: `olai-plugin-kolu`, `olai-plugin-odu` and `olai-plugin-xyne-spaces` are named HERE and nowhere else in the tree, and a general package that named one would be refused by src/fence.test.ts before a reviewer had to notice.
//dependencies: The three plugins, and the two things an interface over browser faces cannot avoid. `effect` is for the schemas a contributed member is declared in; `solid-js` is TYPES ONLY — `JSX.Element` is the return of every face a dressing or a chrome slot names, and a type import puts no runtime on any graph. NO `@olai/surface`, deliberately and structurally: surface depends on THIS package, so a dependency back would be the cycle the whole arrangement is shaped to make unrepresentable. NO `@olai/format` for the same reason one floor over — the kind table travels as DATA, handed down by the server, and a floor package that imported the vocabulary would be the format learning what a terminal is.
